concept.title: Paragraphs
concept.abstract:
This section covers the Paragraph style in Markdown— its role as the primary carrier of explanatory, introductory, and transitional prose in any technical document — and four scenarios: a paragraph in a concept topic, a paragraph containing mixed inline character styles, a paragraph placed before the first heading, and a code paragraph. The converter maps each paragraph to a

element inside the classified topic body, extracts the based on the paragraph context, and maps recognized inline character styles to their corresponding DITA inline elements.

conbody.p:
Paragraphs are the fundamental unit of prose communication in any technical publication. They carry three types of content as described below:
Explanatory content that defines concepts and terms
Introductory content that sets the context for the structured elements that follow such as list, workflows, tables, procedures, and images
Transitional content that connects sections and chapters through the document's logic
This prose content is essential not only for readability but for building complete technical context, search discoverability and structural completeness.
conbody.note: A topic consisting only of a list or a table, with no surrounding prose, is a valid but an incomplete piece of technical communication. It is recommended to add the context to such structured elements.
conbody.p: In Markdown, a paragraph consists of one or more consecutive lines of text separated by one or more blank lines. Empty lines define paragraph boundaries, while multiple consecutive blank lines do not create additional paragraphs. Readers recognize paragraphs as distinct blocks of related information in published output, and the converter uses these boundaries to preserve the logical flow of the source content.

The converter maps each Markdown paragraph to a DITA

element within the appropriate topic body. Depending on the surrounding content, the converter classifies the topic as a Concept, Task, Reference, or Troubleshooting topic. It places the generated

elements inside the corresponding , , or . Inline Markdown formatting, such as bold and italic text, is preserved during conversion by mapping it to the equivalent DITA inline elements. Empty lines used only to separate paragraphs do not generate additional DITA elements.
conbody.note: Separate paragraphs with blank lines rather than using manual spacing or multiple empty lines for visual formatting. Use inline Markdown formatting for emphasis within a paragraph, but use headings, lists, and other Markdown constructs when the content represents a different structural element.
